question: The Russian Film Festival advertised at Rome’s Cinema Barberini (21-23 November 2026) is organised by ROSKINO, with support from Russia’s Ministry of Culture and the participation of the Russian Embassy and the Russian House in Rome1, which has links to Rossotrudnichestvo, listed under Regulation (EU) No 269/20142.

Two scheduled films credit Rossiya as co-producer; its parent company VGTRK and producer Anton Zlatopolskiy are also listed. The event therefore raises questions beyond cultural exchange in the context of Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and its hybrid campaigns against the EU. Considering the above, the Commission is asked: 1.

How will it assess whether venue, licensing, technical or organisational services connected with the festival could make funds or economic resources available, directly or indirectly, to listed persons or entities, contrary to Regulation (EU) No 269/2014?
Does Article 2f of Regulation (EU) No 833/20143 apply to any planned screening, retransmission or online dissemination of the films, and under what conditions?

Will the Commission urgently liaise with the Italian authorities to ensure that all necessary measures are taken, including suspension or cancellation of the event where required by EU law, and that any relevant security vulnerabilities are assessed?
